name: cron-field
title: Cron field
description: A cron field that explains itself: type 0 9 * * 1-5 and read “At 09:00, Monday to Friday”, with the next runs listed in your time zone.
docs: value and onValueChange speak the expression as typed, with { valid } as a second argument: valid is true once the expression is complete and every field is right. A cron expression has five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) and the parser reads * and ?, numbers, lists (1,15), ranges (1-5), steps (*/15 and 10-40/10), JAN to DEC and SUN to SAT, the @hourly, @daily, @weekly, @monthly and @yearly shortcuts, and 7 as Sunday. Under the input the five fields are drawn apart so the reading can be seen, and a sentence says what the expression does in plain English. The sentence is English whatever the locale, the names of the days and months included, so it never mixes two languages; locale decides whether the clock is written on 12 or 24 hours (in the sentence and in the menu of schedules) and how the dates and the distances in the list of runs are written, and a locale that is not a language tag, such as en_US, is read as en-US. Where a schedule runs in bursts it says so (Every 15 minutes during every 2nd hour) and a window runs from the first run to the last (from 09:00 to 17:45). A field that is wrong is named in words (Minute must be 0 to 59) and marked in the drawing, but only once its word is finished: while the caret is still in the last word nothing is flagged, and a field that is not focused is always judged. timeZone sets the clock the schedule follows (an IANA name, default UTC) and the next runs, count of them (default 3), are worked out and written on it, each with how far away it is (in 15 minutes, in 6 hr 15 min, tomorrow, in 3 days). A time that daylight saving skips is left out and a time that happens twice is listed once. now fixes the moment the runs are counted from (a Date, a timestamp or an ISO string); without it the browser's clock is read after mount and again every half minute, so the server and the browser never disagree. presets replaces the menu of six schedules ({ label, value }[]) or turns it off with false. Like the other fields it never blocks a submit; the parser, describeCron and nextRuns are plain functions in cron-field/cron, for a server to check an expression with the same rules.
